reading.title: Understanding venue and billing terms
reading.text: A workplace English worksheet compares venue descriptions. Sports bar emphasizes sports viewing; dive bar is an informal label for an unpretentious bar. Wine bar specializes in wine, while speakeasy may describe a historical illicit venue or a modern venue inspired by that style. Rooftop bar identifies location. Tiki bar describes a themed design rather than authentic representation of all Pacific cultures. Pub, tavern, brewpub and lounge have different regional uses; brewpub combines brewing and hospitality. Happy hour is a promotional period, and last call announces an approaching end to service. A tab is an open bill, a tip additional money for service, and a round of drinks a set ordered for a group. The learner asks about the actual bill and policies without assuming a promotion, tipping rule or opening time is universal.

reading.title: Comparing event activities and charges
reading.text: The learner reads a fictional event announcement. A toast is a message of goodwill; cheers can accompany it and also means thank you in some British usage. A designated driver is assigned to avoid alcohol and drive the group, while fitness to drive remains necessary. Bar tab records purchases, and cover charge names an admission fee separate from orders. Live music involves performers; karaoke involves singing with accompaniment. Trivia night is a quiz event. Dart board and pool table name game equipment, and a jukebox offers recorded-music selection. Comedy night presents comedy; open mic allows participants to sign up for short performances. Dance floor and big screen describe venue features. The learner checks the announcement rather than assumes that one photograph proves the schedule, entry cost or anyone's participation.

reading.title: Interpreting responsible-service language
reading.text: The learner interprets a venue-policy example rather than receives a personal drinking plan. Moderation concerns limiting an amount, ride share a booked transport option, and water break a pause for water. Know your limit is a general message, not an objective test of fitness to drive. Pace yourself means proceed at a controlled rate. Eat before names an action before an activity; food and water do not establish that someone is sober. ID check concerns checking documents, and legal age depends on the activity and jurisdiction. Cut off here means refuse further alcohol service under the venue's rules or law. Choosing an alcohol-free option or declining service is valid. The learner asks which policy applies and arranges transport without relying on a photograph, self-estimated limit or menu label as proof of safety.
